end.summary:
Practised acceleration using a = (v − u)/t, including negative acceleration.
Calculated (10 − 20)/5 = −2 m/s² correctly.
Explained that negative acceleration means speed is decreasing.
Average-speed example: calculated 120 km ÷ 3 h = 40 km/h.
Teach-back was not passed; requested visual motion-lab examples repeatedly.
end.parentNote: Diya practised calculating acceleration, including a braking example with a negative result, and correctly found −2 m/s². Diya continued to mix up the terms “deceleration” and “acceleration” when discussing braking; this was not fully corrected by the end. At home, use a simple number line or toy-car demonstration to show that velocity decreasing can still be called negative acceleration.
